articles.intro: A connected accessory should feel like part of your outfit. Start with the silhouette, then choose the technology that belongs with it.
sections:
01 / Start with one focal point
Choose a watch, a light-led bag, or a sculptural ring. Give one piece the lead and let the rest stay quiet.

02 / Match the finish
Brushed metals sit well beside matte fabric. Polished finishes work as a small contrast against structured tailoring.

03 / Make room at the cuff
A watch reads as an accessory when you can see its shape. Roll a sleeve once, or choose a cropped cuff.

04 / Keep the useful parts close
Before choosing a piece, check the fit, charging routine, and controls. Style works best when the object fits your day.
articles.title: Connected, after dark.

articles.intro: What happens when the handbag becomes a display? The original Tech Noir archive used illuminated couture to open a different conversation about wearable technology.
sections:
The object comes first
A recognisable silhouette gives a new technology a familiar place to live. The details should explain what changes and what stays useful.

Light as a material
Treat illuminated surfaces like colour or jewellery. They shape a look, draw attention, and change with the setting.

The next question
A compelling image starts discovery. Clear details about care, power, fit, and everyday use support the purchase decision.
articles.title: Couture in a digital age

articles.intro: Engineered footwear connects performance and fashion through material, form, and movement.
sections:
Look at the structure
A technical sole can carry the visual weight of an outfit. Pair it with simple trousers and let the construction show.

Understand the material
Knit, leather, and printed structures feel different in motion. A useful product page explains the practical tradeoffs beside the image.

Wear it your way
The styling guide is a starting point. Try the piece with clothing you already own before adding anything else.

products.detail: A quiet silhouette with a connected core. A sapphire-inspired face, activity glance, and discreet notification view bring everyday technology into an evening wardrobe.

products.styling: Wear it just above the wrist bone. Pair the onyx strap with a black cuff, then leave one sleeve slightly raised. Let the brushed metal be the only accent.

products.detail: A familiar frame with discreet audio details. This sample product explores how eyewear can explain a technical feature without losing its fashion identity.
